content.text:
Top 10 recorded entries:

- The Django ORM descriptor example says `QuerySet._fetch_all` calls `self._iterable_class(self)` and that a `djangoResolver` can resolve the attribute to `ModelIterable.__iter__`, producing a `_fetch_all → __iter__ → execute_sql` flow. The relevant files named are `src/resolution/types.ts`, `src/resolution/index.ts`, and `src/resolution/frameworks/python.ts`.

- CodeGraph 0.9.9 improved ranking so common words in a query no longer hijack results, made `codegraph_node` return every matching definition for ambiguous names, and changed `codegraph_explore` so truncated output always drops whole methods or whole files instead of cutting off a method body. Large overload sets now show the most relevant definitions in full and list the rest by location.

- User documented a Tier B backlog for backend command/event/message buses, covering MediatR/CQRS in .NET, Celery in Python, Sidekiq in Ruby, Spring events in Java, and Laravel events in PHP. Each shape has a canonical flow, shipped status, validation repositories, precision notes, and deferred recall items.

- Python dependency tracking now records names imported with `from module import X` even when `X` is only stored in a list or dict, passed as an argument, used as a decorator, or re-exported through an `__init__.py`. Previously Python only linked imports that were called or instantiated, so value-only consumption could look invisible.

- User’s intended Django resolver implementation detects Django via `requirements.txt`, `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, or `manage.py`, resolves `Model`, `View`, `ViewSet`, and `Form` references by name and kind, and returns framework-originated resolutions with confidence 0.8.

- CodeGraph now indexes Dart top-level `const` and `final` values, plus class `static const` and `static final` constants, as constants that participate in constant-reader impact analysis. Instance fields, `var`s, and locals are not treated as constants, and generated Dart files with `.g.dart`, `.freezed.dart`, or `.pb.dart` suffixes are skipped.

- CodeGraph fixed first-sync indexing on very large repositories so it no longer aborts with a "too many SQL variables" error. This fix is tracked as #540.

- User wants `codegraph/CLAUDE.md`’s “Retrieval performance & dynamic-dispatch coverage” doctrine read first and treated as the governing constraint for the proposed fixes.

- User’s backlog discipline says each synthesizer should be validated on at least two real repositories that actually contain the pattern, because a synthesizer tuned on one repo alone is considered unvalidated. The validation repos should be chosen by grepping for the pattern first, not by reputation.

- User’s current implementation uses a whole-graph pass after base resolution rather than a `FrameworkResolver.resolve()` hook, because callback dispatch has no named reference to resolve and requires correlating registrar, registration, and dispatcher across files and sites. The design also distinguishes this from named attribute/descriptor dispatch, which remains handled by `claimsReference` plus a Django ORM resolver.

Each shape has a canonical flow, shipped status, validation repositories, precision notes, and deferred recall items.

- User documented a search-relevance fix where including the project name in a query no longer buries the relevant codebase area; project-name words derived from `go.mod`, `package.json`, or the repo directory are dropped from path scoring and `codegraph_explore` type-disambiguation bias unless they are the only term.

- User wants `codegraph/CLAUDE.md`’s “Retrieval performance & dynamic-dispatch coverage” doctrine read first and treated as the governing constraint for the proposed fixes.

- CodeGraph 0.9.9 improved ranking so common words in a query no longer hijack results, made `codegraph_node` return every matching definition for ambiguous names, and changed `codegraph_explore` so truncated output always drops whole methods or whole files instead of cutting off a method body. Large overload sets now show the most relevant definitions in full and list the rest by location.

- User documented several traps for value-reference-edge work: probe queries must filter `kind='references' AND metadata LIKE '%"valueRef":true%'` because broader `metadata LIKE '%valueRef%'` can match unrelated filenames and create phantom false positives; `searchNodes` returns `SearchResult[]` requiring `.map(r => r.node)`; `getImpactRadius().nodes` is a `Map` that should be iterated with `.values()`; and `CodeGraph.initSync(dir, opts)` ignores `opts` and indexes only `.ts`, `.tsx`, and `.js`.

- User’s Rust coverage includes Axum chained methods and namespaced handlers, Rocket attribute macros, crates.io named Axum routes, cargo-workspace module resolution, and actix builder API routes via `.to(h)`/`.route(...)`; actix scope prefix handling and anonymous closures remain frontier work.

- User documented that Kotlin value-reference coverage required combining multiple techniques: extracting nested property names from `property_declaration`, classifying top-level and `object`/`companion object` properties as constants or variables, class instance properties as fields, adding `simple_identifier` to the reader scan, and pruning `property_declaration` shadows.

- User documented the project’s Git and PR workflow for this work: branch off `main` such as `feat/value-refs-<lang>`, keep pure-validation changes as docs plus a test, keep precision fixes as focused code PRs, use the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>`, add the PR body trailer `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`, and do not self-merge unless authorized.

- User pointed to `value-reference-edges-playbook.md` as the step-by-step runbook for extending value-reference coverage to another language, including wiring, validation scripts, false-positive hunts, declarator types, traps, and the decision of whether the language’s constants are file/module scope or class scope.

content.text:
Top 10 recorded entries:

- User’s backlog discipline says each synthesizer should be validated on at least two real repositories that actually contain the pattern, because a synthesizer tuned on one repo alone is considered unvalidated. The validation repos should be chosen by grepping for the pattern first, not by reputation.

- User documented the changelog rule for this work: user-facing entries belong under `## [Unreleased]`, and a version block should not be pre-created.

- User explicitly marked CommonJS require bindings as intended value-reference edges, not false positives, and said they should not be fixed away.

- The playbook defines five recurring dynamic-dispatch shapes with a difficulty gradient: named attribute/descriptor access in Django, field-backed observers, string-keyed EventEmitter patterns, inline callback handlers, and closure-collection dispatch such as Swift validators. It distinguishes resolvers for named references from synthesizers for anonymous or indirect callbacks.

- The playbook explicitly says the deep design for callback edge synthesis lives in `callback-edge-synthesis.md`, the cross-cutting dispatch-shape queue lives in `dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md`, and the broader investigation context and findings are tracked in the auto-memory `project_codegraph_read_displacement`.

- User documented a Tier B backlog for backend command/event/message buses, covering MediatR/CQRS in .NET, Celery in Python, Sidekiq in Ruby, Spring events in Java, and Laravel events in PHP. Each shape has a canonical flow, shipped status, validation repositories, precision notes, and deferred recall items.

- User fixed C++ override bridging by adding support for C++ `base_class_clause` inheritance edges and a `cpp-override` synthesizer channel, allowing override traces such as `Iterator::Next/Seek/Prev → MergingIterator` in leveldb; the integration test passes.

- User's precision guards for value-reference emission are ordered as: skip generated files via `isGeneratedFile(path)`, then apply shadow pruning, then enforce the distinctive-name and same-file rules. The generated-file check is path-only and cannot detect content-minified bundles.

- User noted that comparing declarator count against file-scope node count, rather than using a flat `>1` rule, preserves conditional module definitions such as `try: X=…; except: X=…`, which legitimately bind the same name twice at file scope. This closes a false-positive class that simple shadow checks would mishandle.

- User documented a deterministic validation recipe for value-refs: index the same repo twice with and without `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0`, confirm node counts match, query edges where `kind='references'` and metadata contains `"valueRef":true`, then inspect the top same-file reader targets and hunt for minified files or re-declared names.

content.text:
Top 10 recorded entries:

- User’s function-as-value capture covers many language-specific value positions, including C/ObjC initializers and `@selector`, C++ `&fn` and `&Cls::method`, TS/JS `this.method`, Python `self.method`, Go expression lists and keyed elements, Rust field initializers, Java method references, Kotlin callable references, C# method groups, Ruby `method(:sym)`, Swift `#selector`, Scala eta-expansion, Dart literals, Lua/Luau callbacks, Pascal event wiring, and PHP callable HOF strings and tuples.

- User documented that value-reference-edge coverage was already validated in TS, JS, TSX, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, and C#, with clean S/M/L runs, identical node counts on and off, and reproduced impact wins; Go, C, Java, and C# each required language-specific extractor or prune adjustments.

- User explicitly marked CommonJS require bindings as intended value-reference edges, not false positives, and said they should not be fixed away.

- CodeGraph now records callback registration sites as reference edges, including function names passed as arguments, function pointers, struct initializers, handler tables, and language-specific forms such as C/C++ `&fn`, Java `Class::method`, Kotlin `::fn`, Swift `#selector`, Objective-C `@selector`, Ruby `method(:fn)`, Scala eta-expansion, and Delphi/Pascal event wiring.

- User documented the Pascal trap that some extractors emit parameters and fields as `variable` at the wrong scope, causing noisy file-wide targets like `Dest` and `aItem`. The fix is to restrict Pascal value-ref targets to `constant` only, while accepting a small residual parse-fidelity caveat where tree-sitter-pascal can misparse a `const` parameter as `declConst`.

- User's plan includes adding `getApplicableFrameworks(detected, language)` in `src/resolution/frameworks/index.ts` so framework resolvers are filtered by language, with resolvers that omit `languages` treated as universal.

- User’s README classification for the chained-call mechanism separates covered languages from skipped ones: covered are C++, C, PHP, Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, Rust, Go, Scala, Dart, Objective-C, and Pascal/Delphi; skipped are TypeScript and Luau; and Python is only partially related via a separate optional `-> T` hint mechanism tracked as #578.

- User documented that the current `VALUE_REF_LANGS` set includes TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, C#, PHP, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Pascal, and that `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` disables the feature.

- User’s precision rules for function-as-value capture include same-file or imported-binding gating, ungated C file-scope initializer handling, TS/JS/Python bare identifiers resolving only to functions, class-scoped handling for `this.X` and `self.m`, C++ requiring explicit `&` except at file scope, Swift refusing ambiguous overload families, skipping forwarded locals like `this.status = status`, ignoring destructuring, excluding generated or minified files, and requiring exact same-language-family, same-file-first resolution with ambiguity producing no edge.

- User documented a Pascal/Delphi fix where calls inside standalone procedures or functions defined only in the `implementation` section are now attributed to that routine instead of the whole file, so callers, impact, and trace can identify the responsible routine; existing indexes need re-indexing with `codegraph index -f`.

item.text:
These are the explicit constraint-like entries I found in project memory, deduplicated:

- `codegraph/CLAUDE.md`’s “Retrieval performance & dynamic-dispatch coverage” doctrine is the governing constraint
- Each synthesizer must be validated on at least two real repositories that actually contain the pattern
- Validation repos should be chosen by grepping for the pattern first, not by reputation
- Branch off `main`, keep pure-validation changes as docs plus a test, keep precision fixes as focused code PRs, and do not self-merge unless authorized
- User-facing changelog entries belong under `## [Unreleased]`, and a version block should not be pre-created
- The dynamic-dispatch mission is not done until canonical flows trace end to end, Read 0 appears in at least some runs with the glue present, there is no node explosion or regression, and the validating repo plus numbers are recorded in the coverage matrix before ship-prep
- The value-reference-edge playbook requires an OSS-only evaluation rule, plus adding a matrix row and a test case before opening a PR
- CommonJS `require` bindings are intended value-reference edges, not false positives, and should not be fixed away
- Value-reference emission must first skip generated files, then apply shadow pruning, then enforce distinctive-name and same-file rules
- The generated-file check is path-only and cannot detect content-minified bundles
- Parameter-only shadowing is a known limitation that is intentionally not guarded yet
- Synthesized callback edges are additive rather than replacing static edges, and over-approximation across instances is acceptable
- Precision is required on control repositories that lack a shape, and a synthesizer should produce 0 false edges there while still producing non-zero precise edges on at least two matching repositories
- Pascal value-ref targets must be restricted to `constant` only
- Intra-file shadowing, especially in bundled, minified, or generated files, is a known false-positive source
- Same-file mutable state and CommonJS `require` bindings are intended cases, not noise
- Function-as-value capture must follow the recorded language-specific precision rules, including same-file/import gating, C file-scope initializer handling, explicit `&` in C++, ambiguity refusal in Swift, and exclusion of generated or minified files
- The markup parser validation plan requires tests for `.cshtml` `@model`, `.razor` component tags, and an HTML non-edge case, plus re-measuring coverage and checking for regressions on control repos
- The current `VALUE_REF_LANGS` set is fixed to the recorded language list, and `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` disables the feature
- The Pascal/Delphi routine-attribution fix requires re-indexing with `codegraph index -f`

If you want, I can also turn this into a two-column table with `title` and `what it constrains`.
